subject.title: Browser: add explicit import from existing-session profile into managed openclaw profile

question: Should OpenClaw support explicitly copying signed-in existing-session browser state into a managed `openclaw` browser profile?
rationale: The code path is clear, but only maintainers can decide whether crossing the current profile-isolation boundary is acceptable and what consent, safe-copy, and rollback constraints are required.

options.title: Approve scoped import
options.body: Implement a one-shot local same-user import with explicit consent, destination reset, transient-file filtering, source untouched, and docs/tests covering the security boundary.

options.title: Reject profile copying
options.body: Keep existing-session attach as the supported way to use logged-in browser state and preserve the managed `openclaw` profile as isolated by design.

options.title: Defer for security design
options.body: Keep the issue open until a short design covers profile artifacts, platform lock files, password-manager or sync state, and rollback behavior.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped import
recommendation.body: Implement a one-shot local same-user import with explicit consent, destination reset, transient-file filtering, source untouched, and docs/tests covering the security boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest merged history across the bundled browser plugin, existing-session support, and the profile/security boundary involved here.
